quirks: Although Mexicans use two surnames, most indexed records carry only the first (paternal) surname — search with the paternal surname alone; when the person is not found, search through the parents (a parent search with each parent's first surname, leaving out the child's name). (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org)
The typical Spanish name has four parts: two given names, the father's surname and the mother's surname. (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Naming_Customs)
localities.guide_markdown:
## Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico - 1880-1920

Although Mexicans use two surnames, most indexed records carry only the first (paternal) surname — search with the paternal surname alone; when the person is not found, search through the parents (a parent search with each parent's first surname, leaving out the child's name). (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org)
